whenToUse: There are six or more options that would take a lot of room laid out.
Lists people already know, such as regions, countries, or years.
It must match the height of other inputs in a form.
whenNotToUse: There are two to five options to compare (use a radio group).
The list is so long people need to search it (use a combobox).

alternatives.name: Radio Group
alternatives.reason: Few enough options to lay out.

alternatives.name: Combobox
alternatives.reason: Long enough that people need to type to find one.

accessibility: It's a native select, so keyboard use, first-letter jumping, and screen reader support come from the browser.
Before a choice, show an unselectable placeholder option.
The arrow icon is decorative, so it's aria-hidden and doesn't block clicks.
